Despite facing a second trade secrets lawsuit over its hardware ambitions in just over a year, OpenAI is still planning to unveil its first product this year and launch it commercially in 2027, according to Bloomberg. Here are the details.

The first product's unveiling timeline remains unchanged at 2026

Last Friday, Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, accusing the company and several former Apple employees of stealing confidential hardware information to advance OpenAI's consumer device plans.

The lawsuit documents detail a pattern of theft of Apple trade secrets by former OpenAI employees, alleging that 'such misconduct has become routine, and is led by example from the company's leadership.'

Following an earlier lawsuit from startup iyO, this new suit adds to OpenAI's legal entanglements in its hardware business. That lawsuit initially focused on branding issues but was later amended to include allegations of trade secret misappropriation.

Despite last Friday's lawsuit news, OpenAI appears to be sticking with its hardware timeline. According to Bloomberg:

Since announcing its partnership with Jony Ive's io Products to develop an 'AI-first' device, speculation has swirled about what OpenAI actually has planned.

After the partnership was announced in May 2025, analyst Ming-Chi Kuo promptly indicated that OpenAI's first device would be a compact, screenless wearable designed to be worn around the neck, equipped with cameras and microphones to capture the user's surroundings, with computation and display functions handled by a smartphone.

OpenAI, meanwhile, has hinted at multiple devices rather than a single product, and stated in legal documents in the iyO lawsuit that its first product is not the in-ear or wearable form factor that外界 speculated when the partnership was announced.
